title: World Wide Web from CERN information pressure to open standards and browser diffusion
pressure: CERN collaborations had heterogeneous computers and information systems; researchers needed linked documents without learning every machine/database interface.
preExistingWorldModel: Internet connectivity and hypertext existed separately; several Internet information systems competed in the early 1990s.
observationsAndInstruments: Berners-Lee proposed the Web in 1989 and implemented server/browser/HTML/HTTP/URL components.
A line-mode browser broadened machine access.
CERN released Web software royalty-free/publicly in 1993.
W3C later coordinated open Web standards.
decisiveTests: resolve and retrieve cross-machine links over existing Internet
independent servers/clients interoperate without central approval
technicalOrScientificTransition: The Web combined existing technologies into a low-friction open information layer; portability, release policy and browser complements converted a laboratory tool into a global platform.
rivalsAndFailures: The Web was not the only Internet information system.
The original NeXT browser was not itself broadly deployable.
Open interfaces enabled diffusion while reducing central control over evolution.
diffusionAndScaling: Diffusion depended on complements, cost/yield/standards and institutional adoption; the nominal breakthrough date did not equal broad effective use.
standardsAndInstitutions: Laboratories, firms, standard bodies, regulators, users and infrastructure operators owned different parts of evidence, implementation and consequence.
externalitiesAndCorrections: Lifecycle harms and authority changes are preserved where evidenced rather than inferred from local technical success.
secondOrderEffects: The Web combined existing technologies into a low-friction open information layer; portability, release policy and browser complements converted a laboratory tool into a global platform.
sourceNativeSummary: The Web combined existing technologies into a low-friction open information layer; portability, release policy and browser complements converted a laboratory tool into a global platform.
unresolvedHistoricalQuestions: Which complement most constrained diffusion at each lifecycle phase?
Which later narrative compresses materially distributed work?
